neighbours.label: An inclusion verb introducing the contents of a work, collection or scope (includes, including, covers, contains), in descriptive or scholarly prose, vs the same subject described without listing contents
fire: His second book, published in 1902, includes a long essay on the Roman roads of Gaul.
The archive holds many rare documents, including letters from the early settlers.
Her survey of medieval law includes a chapter on the trial of animals.
The atlas covers the whole of the Balkan peninsula in remarkable detail.
Ptolemy's treatise includes the coastline of northern Africa as far as the Atlas.
The exhibition shows several early instruments, including a brass astrolabe.
The 1851 edition of the dictionary includes an appendix on regional dialects.
The study examined many coastal towns, including some that were later abandoned.
quiet: His second book, published in 1902, is a long essay on the Roman roads of Gaul.
The archive is famous for its rare documents and letters from the early settlers.
Her survey of medieval law was praised for its chapter on the trial of animals.
The atlas was printed in Vienna and sold widely across the Balkan peninsula.
Ptolemy's treatise was copied by monks in northern Africa for centuries.
The exhibition opened last week and drew large crowds to the brass astrolabe.
The 1851 edition of the dictionary was reprinted three times in Boston.
The study examined many coastal towns, and some were later abandoned.

predictions: Best guess: ' includes'/' including'/' covers' reach 0.3; the same subject without an inclusion verb stays under 0.1. Probes only reached 0.09-0.11, so a failure is expected.
